page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-32xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical Intel Xeon 6455B cores. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and utilizes an x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 11388.44 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds at 480.81 GB/sec. Passmark testing places its database operations, encryption, and extended instructions in the top 10% of tested systems. Additionally, Redis SET operations reach 155.31 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the r7iz.metal-32xl offers high memory capacity paired with high-frequency processing, making it highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring rapid memory access without the overhead of virtualization. However, the lack of bundled local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached options, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. Given its high-frequency Intel Xeon cores and massive DDR5 memory footprint, this instance is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, real-time data processing, and high-throughput web serving.
